title: When the Songbook Wakes
premise: Elodie Yarrow inherited Bellhollow Vineyard buried in debt, and she has kept it afloat by ghostwriting hit love songs under a borrowed name while refusing to sing her own. When a clerical error places her childhood friend turned rival developer, Jonah Reyes, as co-owner of her orchard deed, the two are forced to share the land neither can afford to lose. As Elodie's ghostwriting secret threatens to surface and a predatory label moves to seize Bellhollow, she must decide whether to protect her anonymity or use her true voice to save the vineyard and the man she once loved. She finally claims her name, her song, and Jonah, saving Bellhollow through a public performance that exposes the label's fraud.
about_author: Emrys Thackeray is the pen name of a former orchard hand who spent a decade writing love letters for other people before turning to fiction. Known for stories about quiet people with loud hearts, Emrys writes from a converted cider barn in the foothills.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She opens a county envelope expecting a foreclosure notice and instead finds a deed naming her and Jonah Reyes as co-owners of Bellhollow's orchard. The emotional beat is stunned dread: the past she buried has returned with legal standing.

chapters.title: Ghost Notes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flashback-adjacent chapter revealing she ghostwrites chart-topping songs for pop star Cassa Delacroix, trading her voice for the money keeping the vineyard alive. Beat: the cost of invisibility, and the first crack in her resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Came Back Wrong
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He arrives at Bellhollow with surveyors and a development proposal, claiming the deed is his route to redemption after a bankruptcy of his own. Beat: old love curdled into wary negotiation, neither willing to say what the orchard really means.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They sign an uneasy 60-day co-ownership agreement: she keeps the vines, he evaluates the land for a resort buyout. Beat: a truce built on mutual suspicion, charged by a near-touch over the kitchen table.

chapters.title: Cassa Wants a Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Her label contact demands a new single in three weeks and hints Cassa wants to 'collaborate' publicly, threatening Elodie's anonymity. Beat: the two worlds she kept separate begin to collide.

chapters.title: What the Rows Remember
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Working the vines together, Jonah finds Elodie's old songbook hidden in the cellar and recognizes a melody he's heard on the radio. Beat: dawning wonder and the temptation to confront her before he's sure.

chapters.title: The Buyer in the Tasting Room
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A sleek representative from Meridian Development, Jonah's old employer, tours the vineyard and lets slip that the deed error was engineered. Beat: Elodie realizes Jonah may be a pawn in a larger land grab.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Rain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Elodie accuses him of setting her up; he denies it and, cornered, reveals he knows the songbook is hers. Beat: the secret is out, trust shatters, and the rain makes the confession almost tender.

chapters.title: Silence Has a Price
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She retreats into work, but the label threatens to void her contract and reveal her identity unless she delivers the single. Beat: loyalty to her own survival versus the truth she owes Jonah and herself.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Jonah and Elodie, unable to sleep, meet among the trees and speak honestly for the first time: about the summer they loved each other, the letter he never sent, the song she never finished. Beat: rekindling, fragile and unclaimed.

chapters.title: Paperwork and Poison
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He digs into Meridian's filings and finds the forged signature that created the dual deed, and evidence the label and developer share an owner. Beat: justice outside the law becomes necessary, because every legal door is bought.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The label delivers her single to Cassa, but the demo leaks online and a journalist starts asking who wrote it. Beat: the noose of anonymity tightening as the vineyard's debt notice arrives the same day.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finally gives Elodie the ten-year-old letter, and she reads the truth of why he left. Beat: grief and forgiveness entwined; the past tense of their love begins shifting to present.

chapters.title: Meridian Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Meridian offers to erase her debt if she signs over the orchard and lets them use her ghostwriting identity as a publicity asset. Beat: the career that saved everything is weaponized against her.

chapters.title: A Vote of Two
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Co-ownership means neither can sell without the other; Jonah formally refuses Meridian, burning his own financial rescue. Beat: loyalty chosen over safety, and Elodie watching him do it.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The journalist publishes: Elodie Yarrow is the voice behind Cassa's hits. The label calls it breach of contract; the town calls it a miracle. Beat: humiliation and liberation arriving in the same hour.

chapters.title: What the Contract Couldn't Hold
chapters.summary: Jonah and Elodie's POV alternating. With the label suing and Meridian moving to foreclose, they find the forged deed signature in Meridian's own archived filings. Beat: the plan forms, use her voice, publicly, to expose the fraud before the auction.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Riot
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The town rallies: harvest festival as cover, the auction as the stage, Jonah's evidence as the setlist. Beat: fear transmuted into purpose; Elodie writes the first song in her own name in a decade.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Meridian bids on Bellhollow before a packed hall; Elodie steps onstage, sings her own song, and the forged signature is projected behind her. Beat: the climax, truth as a weapon louder than any lawyer.

chapters.title: Aftermath in C Major
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The fraud unravels, the sale voids, the label settles to avoid scandal, and Cassa publicly credits her. Beat: vindication that feels strangely quiet; the question is no longer survival but what she wants.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Deed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They amend the deed deliberately this time, keeping the orchard together, and plant a new row of vines named for the song. Beat: love declared in the present tense, rooted in shared ground.

chapters.title: When the Songbook Wakes
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A year later: her debut album under her own name, the harvest brought in, Jonah at the mixing desk in the cider barn. Beat: resolution and echo, the woman who stayed invisible singing at last, and being seen.
